newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Launch concerns unsettle Br Biotech.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Launch concerns unsettle Br Biotech.

text.p: The leading light of the UK's biotechnology sector, British Biotech Plc, announced annual losses of 28.9 million pounds ($48.8 million) on Wednesday as it gears up to launch two key products.

The company said losses rose from 25.2 million pounds a year earlier as it funded extensive late-stage trials for anti-cancer drug Marimastat and started to build a sales force for pancreatitis drug Zacutex, which it hopes to launch in Europe next year.

Although losses were well within expectations, British Biotech caused some nervousness among investors over the timing of the launch of the drugs, whose prospects underpin its 1.1 billion pound valuation.

Worries that Zacutex's debut in the important U.S. market could be a year later than expected, and that Marimastat could be at least six months behind some estimates, pushed the shares to a 12-month low of 170 pence during the morning.

By late afternoon they had rallied but were still down by over five percent at 188.5 pence, 12.5p lower, adding to falls seen over the past few weeks. The shares are more than a third below their 1997 peak.
The Oxford-based company's biggest hope is cancer pill Marimastat, the first of a new generation of cancer drugs known as MMP inhibitors.

British Biotech said it was starting late-stage trials of Marimastat in two additional cancers, non-small cell lung cancer and ovarian cancer. It also plans to try the drug in combination with chemotherapy drugs and in slower-acting cancers like breast and colo-rectal.

Marimastat is already being tested in small cell lung, brain, stomach and pancreatic cancers. However news that there was unlikely to be any information from the trials before 1999 disappointed some analysts.
"That is too long," said Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum, who has downgraded his stance on the stock to a sell from a hold.
"I am not prepared to put a billion pound valuation on a drug that is two years away from telling me if it works or not."
Changes to the focus of U.S. trials of Zacutex, which could delay its launch there until 2000, also caused some controversy.
However Greig Middleton analyst John Savin said the decision to extend the U.S. Zacutex trials to cover 1500 patients instead of 450 and compare death rates with placebo would lead to stronger data.
"That is a hard-nosed, big company decision to get the best possible indication and go for the maximum market," he said.

One thing the market will have to adjust to is a period of relative quiet from British Biotech, which has kept up a steady flow of news on products to attract investors. The company indicated that deals to license in drugs from other companies could be the main source of news in the near term.

Chief executive Keith McCullagh told Reuters the company would not "shower the market with news." "We believe we have two excellent drugs in Phase III, with one going through registration. We think the market can judge the size and potential of these drugs." ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
